# Agency product fit (decision support)

## Scope

DevConnect Labs GSE scenario analyzer is **decision-support only**. It uses bundled public-rule summaries and sample FHFA limits — not DU/LPA/TOTAL/GUS, not pricing, not approval, not Ginnie pool eligibility.

## Agencies

- **Fannie Mae** — Conventional conforming; Selling Guide; products such as HomeReady.
- **Freddie Mac** — Conventional conforming; Seller/Servicer Guide; products such as Home Possible.
- **FHA** — HUD Handbook 4000.1; government-insured; may support Ginnie Mae MBS after issuer pooling.
- **VA** — VA Pamphlet 26-7; guaranteed; may support Ginnie Mae MBS after issuer pooling.
- **USDA** — HB-1-3555; rural guaranteed; may support Ginnie Mae MBS after issuer pooling.
- **Ginnie Mae** — MBS guarantor for government loans; not an underwriting agency.

## Overlays

Lender/investor overlays can tighten agency minimums (credit, LTV, reserves, property type). Overlay findings are operational risk signals — always confirm current investor matrices.

## FHFA loan limits

Conforming loan limits vary by county and unit count. High-cost areas may have higher ceilings. Bundled limit JSON is a sample year snapshot — verify fhfa

records.title: Arm First Rate Change (1/2)
records.content:
# ARM first rate change date

## Definitions

- **First rate change date** — First date the ARM note interest rate can adjust. Not the first borrower payment after closing, and not the MBS pool issue date.
- **First payment change date** — First due date of the new principal-and-interest payment after a rate adjustment.

## Usual note math

On typical agency ARMs, rate and payment do not move on the same day:

**1st interest rate change date ≈ 1st payment change date − 1 month**

Examples:

- Rate change **March 1** → payment change **April 1**
- Rate change **June 1** → payment change **July 1**

Fannie loan-delivery job aids often calculate the interest rate change date as the 1st payment change date minus one month. Initial fixed period (e.g. 60 months on a 5/1) is commonly measured from first payment date to first interest rate change date.

ARM Flex MBS pools generally require payment due dates on the first of the month; odd due dates need a negotiated contract.

## Bank / ops cycle cutoff (example)

Some lenders use a calendar cutoff so lookback, rate calculation, Reg Z notices, and boarding still fit before the next payment-change cycle.

The 10th/11th only chooses which cycle the bank books. Inside that cycle, note math (rate month, then payment month) still applies. Cutoffs are investor/servicer-specific — not universal agency guide text.

## Notices (Reg Z)

When a rate adjustment changes the payment, servicers must send disclosures timed from the **first payment at the adjusted level**:

- Initial adjustment: typically 210–240 days before that payment (or at consummation if sooner).
- Subsequent adjustments: typically 60–120 days before (shorter windows for very frequent adjusters).

Index lookback is plan-specific (often on the order of ~45 days before the rate change).

## Verify

Confirm the note, ARM plan, investor matrix, and servicer calendar before locking first rate / payment change dates.

records.title: Mortgage Pooling Mbs (1/4)
records.content:
# Mortgage pooling and MBS

## Overview

After a loan closes, lenders often sell it into the secondary market. **Pooling** groups loans with similar features; **securitization** turns that pool into a mortgage-backed security (MBS). Cash flows (principal and interest) pass through to investors.

## Who pools what

- **Fannie Mae / Freddie Mac (GSEs)** — Conventional conforming loans meeting Selling Guide / Seller/Servicer Guide rules. Issue Agency MBS / UMBS. Guaranty is the enterprise’s obligation, not full faith and credit of the U.S. government.
- **Ginnie Mae** — Does not buy loans or underwrite. Guarantees MBS issued by approved issuers that pool government-insured/guaranteed loans (FHA, VA, USDA/RHS). Full faith and credit of the U.S.
- **Private-label** — Non-agency securitizations; outside typical agency TBA liquidity.

## UMBS, TBA, specified pools

- **UMBS** — Uniform MBS under FHFA Single Security; Fannie and Freddie TBA-eligible fixed-rate pools (10/15/20/30-year) are fungible in one TBA market. Re-securitizations of UMBS are called **Supers**.
- **TBA** — Trade agrees on term, coupon, face, price, settlement; pool/CUSIP announced ~48 hours before settle (48-Hour Rule)

- **TBA** — Trade agrees on term, coupon, face, price, settlement; pool/CUSIP announced ~48 hours before settle (48-Hour Rule). SIFMA good-delivery rules define interchangeable collateral.
- **Specified pools** — CUSIP known at trade; may pay up vs TBA for desirable prepay traits.

## Fannie Mae pooling parameters (summary)

Confirm current Selling Guide Part C3 before delivery.

- **Single-lender pool** — One lender’s loans. Typical minimum aggregate UPB: $1M fixed-rate; $500K ARMs.
- **Fannie Majors** — Multi-lender; once open, small contributions allowed; often ≤12 months seasoning.
- **Note-rate band (fixed-rate)** — Note rates generally from 25 bp to 112.5 bp above pool pass-through.
- **Term buckets** — Common original-term bands: 30-yr 181–360 mo; 20-yr 181–240; 15-yr 85–180; 10-yr 85–120.
- **Ops** — MBS execution approval, document custodian + Master Custodial Agreement (Form 2017), loan delivery data (often ULDD) with certification before pool close.

## Standard vs same-month pooling (first payment)

records.title: Mortgage Pooling Mbs (3/4)
records.content:
- Pool **issue date** is the 1st of the issue month.
- **Standard pooling** — First payment date no later than the 1st of the month immediately after issue (e.g. March 1 issue → first payment on/before April 1).
- **Same-month pooling** — Pool in the same month as origination; first payment may be the 1st of the month two months after issue (e.g. March issue → May 1), with initial interest-only remittance to Fannie because the borrower has not yet paid.
- Separately, first payment must be no later than two months from final disbursement.

## Ginnie Mae pooling (summary)

- **Ginnie Mae I** — Single-issuer pools.
- **Ginnie Mae II** — Custom (single issuer) or multiple-issuer pools from loan packages.
- Pool types include level payment, buydown, ARM, GPM, GEM, serial notes — each with guide chapters and custodian rules.
- Issuers must meet net worth / liquidity tests; electronic pooling required for SF.

## Pass-through economics

Borrower note rate → investor pass-through coupon after servicing fee + guaranty fee (g-fee). Investors receive pro-rata scheduled P&I plus unscheduled principal.

## Verify

Always confirm current Fannie Selling Guide C3, Freddie capital markets / guides
